findings.title: traceID no longer explicitly included in 'Plugin Request Completed' (grafana-data-egress) log lines
findings.body: The old LoggerMiddleware.logRequest explicitly appended a "traceID" field extracted via tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false). The rewrite drops this and relies on whatever the contextual logger injects. If the infra logger's FromContext does not attach a trace id to this log line (or emits it under a different key such as "trace_id"), the data-egress log events lose trace correlation or change field naming, breaking any dashboards, alerts, or log parsers that key on the "traceID" field of these events. This should be verified and, if the field is gone, restored explicitly or the field-name change documented.

findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext returns a brand-new logger, silently discarding logs written through the contextual path
findings.body: TestLogger.FromContext returns NewTestLogger() instead of the receiver, so any log emitted via logger.FromContext(ctx) is written to a throwaway object that no test can inspect. Since LoggerMiddleware.logRequest was changed to call m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...), existing and future tests using TestLogger can no longer assert on the 'Plugin Request Completed' log at all — assertions on InfoLogs will show zero calls while the code under test may be logging correctly, incorrectly, or with missing fields. The fake should return the receiver (f) so tests can actually verify the log output, including whether pluginId/endpoint/uname/dsName/dsUID still appear after this refactor.

findings.title: No tests for the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware or for the contextual log fields of LoggerMiddleware
findings.body: This PR moves responsibility for the pluginId, endpoint, uname, dsName and dsUID log fields from LoggerMiddleware's explicit logParams into a new ContextualLoggerMiddleware that enriches the context. There is no test covering ContextualLoggerMiddleware (e.g., that the context actually carries the expected attributes per endpoint and that stream endpoints are not enriched), nor any test asserting that LoggerMiddleware's output still contains those fields when routed through FromContext. A regression here — wrong middleware ordering in CreateMiddlewares, a dropped attribute, or the grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext type-assertion fallback silently discarding attributes — would go completely unnoticed.

findings.title: Adding FromContext to the exported Logger interface is a compile-time breaking change for external implementers
findings.body: The exported plugins/log.Logger interface gained a required FromContext(ctx context.Context) Logger method. Any implementer of this interface outside this PR (e.g., Grafana Enterprise or other downstream consumers of the public grafana repo, which already had to track the interface for New/Debug/Info/Warn/Error) will now fail to compile until they add the method. If the intent is only internal consumption, consider keeping the base interface unchanged and defining a separate ContextualLogger interface (Logger + FromContext) accepted by LoggerMiddleware, or provide an embedding helper, so existing implementations keep working.
